original.target_description: Shiner, Masten, and Tellegen (2002), single longitudinal cohort; Table 4, adult MPQ Negative Emotionality correlated with concurrent age-20 Conduct (rule-abiding versus antisocial conduct), complete-case participants. This is a located candidate; the supplied locator does not uniquely distinguish childhood from concurrent conduct.

n.sample_role: Participants with complete childhood adaptation, adult adaptation, and adult personality data; analytic subsample for Table 4 correlations.
n.exclusions: Complete-case restriction explicitly stated. Initial cohort 205; specific exclusion reasons beyond incomplete data are not enumerated for this test.
n.location: p. 1171 (PDF p. 7), section “Is Personality in Emerging Adulthood Related to Childhood and Concurrent Adaptation?”, paragraph preceding Table 4
n.quote: These analyses were conducted … with a subsample of 187 participants for whom the childhood … adaptation data and the adult adaptation and personality data were complete.

es.location: p. 1171 (PDF p. 7), Table 4, Negative Emotionality row × Concurrent adaptation / Conduct column

p.location: p. 1171 (PDF p. 7), Table 4, Negative Emotionality row × Concurrent adaptation / Conduct column; three-asterisk table footnote

notes: Published article supplied by licensed EBSCO PsycInfo service; title, authors, year and DOI verified in supplied text. Only original target examined. Statistics are printed correlations with positively scored rule-abiding conduct, not sign-converted correlations with antisocial behavior. Page 1170 states: “the conduct composite was scored in the opposite direction (ranging from poor to good conduct)”. The p value and r refer to the same concurrent Conduct cell. Target match remains unknown because the neutral description and p.7 locator do not explicitly select concurrent versus childhood conduct. Table 4 separately prints Negative Emotionality/childhood Conduct −.21**; the supplied locator does not explicitly disambiguate that longitudinal association from the extracted concurrent association.
